$comment: The core color roles: the vocabulary every system must value. Values never live here — each system's layer file says which tone of which palette a role takes. A role is core because ONE PRODUCT may need that distinction; a role that only one design system has is a declared palette instead (see `palettes` in tokens/systems/*.system.json).

llm.usage: Color ROLES. Components and product UI bind to a role, never to a palette tone or a literal. Roles come in pairs that are contrast-checked together: draw `on-x` content on `x`, and `on-x-container` on `x-container`. Surfaces step from surface-container-lowest to -highest to separate regions without borders.
rules: Choose a role by MEANING (error, success, warning, info, link, focus-ring, outline…), not by the color you expect it to have — a design system may give it any color.

A product-specific meaning (brand, correct/incorrect, a category) is a declared palette in the layer's "palettes" with "roles": "intent": it yields x, on-x, x-container, on-x-container. Do not reuse error/success for it and do not add tokens.
Never hardcode hex values in a product using Tanrei; they will not follow the scheme, the contrast level or the design system.

intent.rationale: One product fills a container with this color, puts content on it, and also uses a quieter container of the same intent.

intents.primary: The product's main action and brand emphasis. Separate from every other intent because a product's brand color is rarely its error, success or link color.
intents.secondary: Lower-emphasis actions and selections (tonal buttons, chips) that must not compete with the primary action.
intents.error: Something failed or is destructive. Every product with a form or a delete button needs it.
intents.success: Something succeeded or is valid: form validation, completed steps, positive status.
intents.warning: Something needs attention before it becomes an error: caution banners, risky choices.
intents.info: Neutral, non-urgent system information, distinct from the brand color so notices do not read as calls to action.

roles.surface: The default background of a view.
roles.surface-dim: A background that recedes behind `surface` (wells, the area around a sheet).
roles.surface-bright: A background that stays bright in dark schemes (bars that must separate from a dark canvas).
roles.surface-container-lowest: The lowest of five container steps. One product nests cards in panels in pages, so it needs several distinguishable steps at once.
roles.surface-container: Container step 3 of 5: the default container.
roles.surface-container-highest: Container step 5 of 5: inputs and chips that sit on other containers.
roles.surface-variant: A differently weighted surface for low-emphasis fills such as tracks.
roles.on-surface: Primary text and icons on any surface.
roles.on-surface-variant: Secondary text and icons: supporting copy, placeholders, inactive icons.
roles.outline: A boundary people must be able to see to identify a control (an input's border, an unchecked checkbox): at least 3:1.
roles.outline-variant: A decorative hairline (dividers, card edges). Separate from `outline` because a product wants quiet dividers without losing visible input borders.
roles.focus-ring: The keyboard focus indicator (its outer stroke). Separate from `primary` because a product may want a saturated brand color and a calmer, or more visible, focus ring.
roles.focus-ring-inner: The optional inner stroke of the focus indicator: a second tone that keeps the indicator visible where the outer one would blend into the background.
roles.link: Inline text links. Separate from `primary` because links sit in running text and must read as links, whatever the brand color is.
roles.inverse-link: Inline text links on `inverse-surface`. Separate from `inverse-primary` for the reason `link` is separate from `primary`: a product whose links are not its brand color needs them told as links on a surface of the opposite theme too, and a layer that re-points `link` and `inverse-link` has recolored every text link and nothing else.
roles.inverse-surface: A surface of the opposite theme inside the current one (snackbars, tooltips).
roles.scrim: Dims content behind a modal surface.
roles.shadow: The color shadows are cast in.
roles.elevation-ring: The hairline ring that edges an elevated surface. Separate from `outline-variant` so a product can outline elevated surfaces more or less strongly than it draws dividers.
